UPSTREAM: drm/ttm: Provide ttm_bo_global_{init/release}() for struct ttm_bo_global So far, struct ttm_bo_global_ref was the only way of initializing a struct ttm_bo_global. Providing separate initializer and release functions for struct ttm_bo_global gives drivers the option of implementing their own init and release callbacks for drm_global_references of type DRM_GLOBAL_TTM_BO. The original functions for initializing and releasing via struct ttm_bo_global_ref are wrappers around the new interfaces. BACKPORT: platform/chrome: Add new driver for Wilco EC This EC is an incompatible variant of the typical Chrome OS embedded controller. It uses the same low-level communication and a similar protocol with some significant differences. The EC firmware does not support the same mailbox commands so it is not registered as a cros_ec device type. This commit exports the wilco_ec_mailbox() function so that other modules can use it to communicate with the EC. BACKPORT: platform/chrome: wilco_ec: Add RTC driver This Embedded Controller has an internal RTC that is exposed as a standard RTC class driver with read/write functionality. The driver is added to the drivers/rtc/ so that the maintainer of that directory will be able to comment on this change, as that maintainer is the expert on this system. In addition, the driver code is called indirectly after a corresponding device is registered from core.c, as opposed to core.c registering the driver callbacks directly. shill: wifi: Examine assoc/auth status codes at disconnect CL:1226113 uses 802.11 disconnect reasons to generate more suitable shill disconnect reasons. However, assoc/auth status codes are still not used. Of particular importance is when a connection fails due to a pending timeout, as supplicant will always see this as a user disconnect (reason 3). Looking at the assoc/auth status codes provides us with more information, allowing for more accurate shill disconnect reasons. This change also uploads the status codes of assoc/auth failures to UMA. main: add --cpu-affinity option to pin VCPUs This allows setting the affinity of the VCPU threads to specific host CPUs. Note that each individual CPU has its affinity set to the full set of CPUs specified, so the host kernel may still reschedule VCPU threads on whichever host CPUs it sees fit (within the specified set). Machines that aren't in a good state may not be left powered on for that long, so we lose the reports from them. Run crash_sender the first time 5 minutes after boot up.
